message:
Plain words: operators cannot see the robot, so forward must always mean the same end or steering inverts. The leading digging end is fixed as forward in the drive camera and the trailing dump end is fixed as rear in the mast view from the blind-operation layout (E34), so reverse-to-bin stays viewpoint-relative; Excavation and Regolith Handling Lead please keep digging leading and dumping trailing as the Manager fixed, because coarse error 0.100 m to 0.150 m from the blind drift simulation (E33) trimmed to 0.030 m to 0.040 m at 1.00 m to 2.00 m by the tag align simulation (E58) only holds if the tag is always sought behind.

Plain words: Mobility and Deployable Chassis Lead is right that a raised load can tip, so blind control must refuse to pour on a slope. I take from the Skid-Steer Safety for Farm and Landscape (E47) the rule that lifting a load transfers weight and raises the balance point, which for blind operation means the Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU, meaning tilt and turn sensor) level check gates the tilt command; pivot 0.550 m clears the 0.400 m lip by 0.150 m with factor 1.69 level-only at 15.0 kg trips from the tip dump clearance check (E51), like a wheelbarrow held flat, so dumping only when level keeps it upright.

Plain words: loss of link must stop motion in a shoe length even though wheels slip blind. Capped speed 0.500 m per s with 0.500 s heartbeat gives 0.308 m total stop from the link-loss simulation (E32) versus 0.0625 m brake-only from the tip-over and stopping check (E23), well under 1 g, and stall backout 0.600 s from the tag align and backout simulation (E58) is a blink against 300 s to warm 18.0 K from the motor heating estimate (E44). Ready, because direction, loss, drift, tip-gate and stall all survive my strongest blind objections with only arching, wear and tag-visibility bench tests left.
